AUDIO IMPORTANT:

if there is no audio in your video-in then it errors. 

If you have silent video, you will need to provide audio in of some kind to run the workflow, even if you dont include it in the output video. Use the audio loader to load in a random mp3 (e.g. 10 seconds of music or ambient silence) and set duration to match your inbound video. swithc the audio vae encoder to use this not the video. This should then work.

NOTE: I found if I prompt for "non_diegetic_music:" it will then use it rather than the audio, so make sure to put "N/A" in any audio descriptors for the prompt if you want to keep the audio you are loading in.

<Subject 2> is the man in <Picture 2>, medium length brown hair, wearing brown leather jacket and blue jeans.
<Subject 3> is the brunette woman in <Picture 3>, wearing black leather pants and a black leather vest top, with wavy dark brown hair.
<Subject 4> is the blonde woman in <Picture 4>, wearing a blue dress with her blonde hair tied up in a bun.
<Subject 5> is the Black woman in <Picture 5>, wearing a leopard-print dress.

<Subject 2> (appears in [Shot 1]): fully_preserved - the man's identity and appearance from <Picture 2> are retained.

<Subject 4> (appears in [Shot 1]): fully_preserved - the blonde woman's blue dress and identity are retained.
<Subject 5> (appears in [Shot 1]): fully_preserved - the Black woman's leopard-print dress and identity are retained.

detailed_description:
The target video is a realistic interior scene shot from in front of the elevator doors, with warm light catching the marble walls and brass door trim.
[Shot 1] A medium group shot establishes <Subject 1>, the marble lobby with its closed brass-toned elevator doors and carved stone surround directly behind the group. The four figures stand together facing the elevator, waiting: <Subject 3>, the brunette in black leather pants and vest, on the far left; <Subject 4>, the blonde in the blue dress, beside her; <Subject 2>, the man, at center; and <Subject 5>, the Black woman in the leopard-print dress, on the right. 

<Subject 5> (S1) tightens her arms across her chest and says with a sarcastic edge, <d>[English] He's drunk, the asshole.</d> <Subject 3> presses her lips together and shakes her head quietly, saying nothing, her eyes flicking toward the man. At 00:03.000, <Subject 4> (S2) tilts her head with a sarcastic smirk and says sharply,<d>[English] Like you aren't high half the time?</d> 
At 00:05.500, <Subject 5> (S1) snaps back, raising one hand in a dismissive, disdainful gesture, <d>[English] Shut up, bitch!</d>
At 00:07.500, <Subject 2> (S3) lowers his gaze, rubs the back of his neck, and says nervously, <d>[English] I may have had a couple of drinks. I was nervous.</d> His shoulders stay tense as he avoids eye contact with the group until the shot ends.

overall_soundscape:
Quiet room tone with a faint distant elevator mechanism sound continues throughout the shot.

N/A

1600 × 640 (1mp)

1120 x 448 (0.50 mp) - 
866 x 346 (0.3mp)
640 x 256 = (0.16mp) - test resolution 150 seconds.

# MarkDKBerry.com

YouTube: [https://www.youtube.com/@markdkberry](https://www.youtube.com/@markdkberry)

Patreon: [https://www.patreon.com/c/AIMakingMovies](https://www.patreon.com/c/AIMakingMovies)

Workflows: [https://github.com/mdkberry/comfyui_workflows](https://github.com/mdkberry/comfyui_workflows)

---

**You will need to install [https://github.com/ckinpdx/ComfyUI-MMH3Tools](https://github.com/ckinpdx/ComfyUI-MMH3Tools) for this workflow.** If you have a Low or MidVRAM (12GB VRAM) card this workflow should work for you, if you have a bigger card, you might want to test ckinpdx upscale workflows instead. 

It works by "context window" splitting the total frames (e.g. 192 frame video split to two segments, so you can get to the magical 2mp for 8 second clips as I did in tests, even on a 3060 RTX. You max VRAM is then used on each split segment thus giving you better reach. Amazingly it was still faster than my other upscaler workflows.

---

**Updated**: 24th August 2026. *(This is the fastest and highest resolution solution to dialogue scene upscaling I have found so far.)*

**Useage**: *Single pass v2v pixel space upscaler with context windows to split use of the VRAM across multiple segments, making higher resolution possible for longer clips on lowerVRAM.*


---

## USING THIS WORKFLOW


**Get a structural video made elsewhere, then import it here for detailing.** (its best if you use fairly high quality result coming in, I found 1824 x 736 was good that needed eyes fixing a bit and blemishes. For stronger fixing, you might need to increase denoise or steps. I havent tested it for that yet.)

**Set to chosen megapixel upscale size I can do 2mp for 8 seconds in this workflow** (see the notes beside the video import node). Resize if you need to reduce the inbound video, upscale if you need to increase it. Size it to fit your VRAM and avoid ooms.

**I've been leaving the width and height of the actual "H3 Reference To Video Model" Node set to 1mp**. We know it to be the size the H3 model was trained on. But the important bit is the size of your inbound video and what you resize that to.

**The frame count of the video-in is used to define the length**, as such the duration has been disabled in this workflow. 

**Since this uses context windows, oom from longer videos is mitigated**. I have only tested 8 seconds long video so far and could get to 2mp with only 10.5GB VRAM being used. There is a spike going into  the sampler but it didnt oom on my setup with this workflow. Context windows is the reason for this. Its suprisingly fast, considering that, I was expecting it to take a lot longer.

**Make a new prompt and be sure to target the ref images correctly**. 

I am getting 8 second video done in 26 mins to 2mp. Longer clip length will probably work too due to the "context windows" from the ckinpdx custom node.

## ISSUES:

- You must provide audio to the workflow either from the inbound video, or by providing your own audio file. I have put a audio loader in there which you can reconnect (yellow vrs red reroute connector).
